title: Recover the optimal buffer vector from residual potentials
problem: R04's maximum-cost circulation certifies the weighted interval-packing optimum but the flow objective is not itself the buffer schedule.
failure: An initial recovery proof said a positive recovered gap implies a reverse residual edge and a saturated gap arc. This inference fails when the gap capacity c_k is zero: the flow is zero and no reverse residual edge exists, although the potential difference can be positive. The theorem is still valid because both objective terms for that gap are zero.
correction: For uncapped interval arcs, use optimal max-profit potentials P with P_v-P_u at least the arc profit on every residual edge, then set g_k=max(0,P_k-P_(k-1)). Positive-flow intervals have tight potential inequalities. For positive gap capacity, residual cases cover zero, interior, and saturated flow; treat c_k=0 separately, where z_k=c_k=0 and both objective contributions vanish without a residual-edge condition. Verify all interval constraints and compare the recovered objective to the circulation value.
transfer: When recovering a primal schedule from network dual potentials, state the sign convention, keep unbounded and capped arcs distinct, and check each residual-capacity case. A bounded solver run can expose sign/index mistakes but does not replace the complementary-slackness proof.
limits: One fixed-order berth-buffer model with nonnegative linear gap prices and uncapped interval arcs. The R05 certificate covers 36 integer and 36 denominator-six rational-grid instances; it does not establish runtime complexity, arbitrary-rational empirical coverage, operational performance, or originality. HORUS was an internal analytical-agent reviewer; no human peer review.
